::: {.home-content .justify}
I am a postdoctoral researcher at [Marburg University, Germany](https://www.uni-marburg.de/de/fb04/team-heck/team/bjoern-siepe), where I recently finished my PhD in Psychological Methods. My [research](../publications) focuses on three areas: metascience of methodological research, time series modelling, and applied experience sampling research. Throughout these, I build open source software tools and try to promote open science practices.

In my work on time series modelling, I develop and evaluate novel multilevel models for time series data, with a particular emphasis on quantifying and communicating uncertainty in model outputs. To help researchers applying these methods, I have (co-)developed multiple [software](../software) packages for R and Python. 

This methodological work influences my metascientific work, where I study how we can conduct methodological research in a transparent, robust, and reproducible way. One result of this work was the introduction of [ADEMP-PreReg](https://github.com/bsiepe/ADEMP-PreReg), a protocol for reporting and preregistering simulation studies. I'm currently (co-)chairing two working groups on quality standards for simulation studies, and I'm always open to chat about novel ideas to improve methodological research.

I have always enjoyed teaching statistics and programming to students and researchers. Over the years, I have given multiple workshops on reproducible research and time series modelling, for which you can find the materials on my [workshop page](../workshops).

I'm committed to open science practices. Together with collaborators, I built [openESM](https://openesmdata.org), an open-source database of 60+ experience sampling datasets. We are actively working on expanding the database and making it easier for researchers to use it. Updates on the project can be found on the [openESM blog](https://openesmdata.org/blog/). I'm also a board member of the [Open Science Initiative](https://openscienceinitiativeuniversitymarburg.github.io/) at Marburg University.
